_comment: Kubernetes `reason` strings → what they mean and what to do. Read by bossman/services/kubernetes.py (explain) and shown wherever a state pill, a pod row or a Warning event carries the reason. The rule it serves: nothing is red without the reader being able to reach WHY (sufficient reason). `doc` points at the kubernetes.io page the explanation is taken from. Add a reason = add an entry; unknown reasons are still shown, just without the explanation.

ImagePullBackOff.title: Image cannot be pulled
ImagePullBackOff.explanation: The node tried to pull the container image and failed; it now retries with a growing delay (up to 5 minutes). The usual causes: the image name or tag is wrong, the image was never pushed, or the registry is private and the pod has no matching imagePullSecret.
ImagePullBackOff.fix: Check the image name and tag in the workload's container (a typo or a tag that does not exist is the most common cause). For a private registry add an image pull secret and reference it in the pod or its ServiceAccount.

ErrImagePull.title: Image pull failed
ErrImagePull.explanation: The most recent attempt to pull the image failed. ImagePullBackOff follows once the retries back off.
ErrImagePull.fix: Same as ImagePullBackOff: verify the image reference, the registry's reachability from the node, and pull credentials.

InvalidImageName.title: Image reference is not valid
InvalidImageName.explanation: The image string cannot be parsed as [registry/]name[:tag][@digest].
InvalidImageName.fix: Correct the image reference; uppercase letters and spaces are not allowed in the repository name.

ErrImageNeverPull.title: Image not present and pulls are disabled
ErrImageNeverPull.explanation: imagePullPolicy is Never and the node does not have the image locally.
ErrImageNeverPull.fix: Pre-load the image on every node, or set imagePullPolicy to IfNotPresent.

CrashLoopBackOff.title: Container keeps crashing
CrashLoopBackOff.explanation: The container starts, exits, and is restarted by the kubelet with a growing delay (10 s, 20 s, 40 s … up to 5 min). The exit code and the previous container's log say why it exits: a missing config or environment variable, a wrong command, a port already in use, or a failing liveness probe.
CrashLoopBackOff.fix: Open the Logs tab with 'previous' to read the crashed container's output. Check the exit code: 1 = application error, 137 = killed (often OOM), 139 = segfault. If a liveness probe is failing, give the app a startup probe or loosen the probe.

OOMKilled.title: Killed for exceeding its memory limit
OOMKilled.explanation: The container used more memory than its limit, so the kernel killed it (exit code 137). The kubelet then restarts it.
OOMKilled.fix: Raise the memory limit, or fix the leak. Check the unit: '400m' means 0.4 BYTES of memory, a classic typo for '400Mi'.

CreateContainerConfigError.title: Container configuration cannot be built
CreateContainerConfigError.explanation: The kubelet could not assemble the container: a referenced ConfigMap or Secret (for env, envFrom or a volume) does not exist in this namespace, or a key is missing.
CreateContainerConfigError.fix: Create the missing ConfigMap/Secret in the pod's namespace, or mark the reference optional.

CreateContainerError.title: Runtime could not create the container
CreateContainerError.explanation: The container runtime refused to create the container — usually an invalid command/args, a missing executable in the image, or an unsupported security setting.
CreateContainerError.fix: Check the container's command and args exist inside the image, and the securityContext is supported by the runtime.

RunContainerError.title: Container failed to start
RunContainerError.explanation: The runtime created the container but it could not be started — for example a volume mount path that is a file, or an entrypoint that is not executable.
RunContainerError.fix: Compare volumeMounts against the image's filesystem and verify the entrypoint.

Unschedulable.title: No node can take this pod
Unschedulable.explanation: The scheduler found no node that satisfies the pod: not enough free CPU/memory for its requests, a nodeSelector/affinity that matches no node, a taint without a toleration, a hostPort already in use, or a volume that is bound to another zone.
Unschedulable.fix: Read the FailedScheduling event: it names each node and why it was rejected. Lower the requests, add nodes, fix the selector, or add the toleration.

FailedScheduling.title: Scheduling failed
FailedScheduling.explanation: The event behind an Unschedulable pod. Its message lists every node and the reason it was rejected (Insufficient cpu, node(s) had untolerated taint, didn't match Pod's node affinity …).
FailedScheduling.fix: Act on the per-node reason in the message.

FailedMount.title: A volume could not be mounted
FailedMount.explanation: A volume the pod needs is not available: a PersistentVolumeClaim that is not bound, a ConfigMap/Secret that does not exist, or a storage backend that refused the mount.
FailedMount.fix: Check the PVC is Bound (Storage → PersistentVolumeClaims) and that referenced ConfigMaps/Secrets exist in the namespace.

FailedAttachVolume.title: A volume could not be attached to the node
FailedAttachVolume.explanation: The storage driver could not attach the volume to the node — often because it is still attached elsewhere (ReadWriteOnce volumes attach to ONE node).
FailedAttachVolume.fix: Wait for the old pod to terminate, or use a ReadWriteMany-capable storage class if several pods on different nodes must share the volume.

Evicted.title: Evicted from the node
Evicted.explanation: The kubelet removed this pod because the node ran out of a resource (memory, disk, PIDs). BestEffort pods (no requests) go first, then Burstable pods exceeding their requests.
Evicted.fix: Set resource requests so the pod has a guaranteed share, and give nodes headroom. The workload controller creates a replacement.

ProgressDeadlineExceeded.title: Rollout stalled
ProgressDeadlineExceeded.explanation: The Deployment did not make progress for progressDeadlineSeconds (default 10 min). Kubernetes does NOT roll back by itself; the Deployment stays in this state until you act. The new pods are usually failing — see the Pods tab.
ProgressDeadlineExceeded.fix: Fix the pods' problem (image, config, probes) or roll back to the previous revision.

BackOff.title: Restart back-off
BackOff.explanation: The kubelet is waiting before restarting a container that keeps failing (the event behind CrashLoopBackOff).

Unhealthy.title: A probe is failing
Unhealthy.explanation: A liveness, readiness or startup probe returned failure. A failing readiness probe removes the pod from its Service; a failing liveness probe restarts the container.
Unhealthy.fix: Check the probe's path/port against what the app actually serves, and its timing (timeoutSeconds 1 s is often too short). Use a startup probe for slow-starting apps.

FailedCreate.title: Pods could not be created
FailedCreate.explanation: The controller asked for pods and the API server refused — typically a ResourceQuota that is exhausted, a LimitRange violation, or a Pod Security admission rejection.
FailedCreate.fix: Read the event message: it quotes the quota/limit/policy that refused. Raise the quota, set requests/limits, or make the pod spec comply with the namespace's Pod Security level.

NotReady.title: Node is not ready
NotReady.explanation: The kubelet reported Ready=False: the node's container runtime, network, or kubelet itself is unhealthy. Pods on it are evicted after the eviction timeout.
NotReady.fix: Check the node's kubelet and runtime logs and its network.

MemoryPressure.title: Node is low on memory
MemoryPressure.explanation: The node's available memory fell below the eviction threshold; new pods are not scheduled here and BestEffort/Burstable pods may be evicted.
MemoryPressure.fix: Reduce the workload on this node or add memory/nodes; set requests so scheduling stays balanced.

DiskPressure.title: Node is low on disk
DiskPressure.explanation: The node's root or image filesystem is above the eviction threshold. Image garbage collection runs; pods may be evicted.
DiskPressure.fix: Free disk on the node (old images, logs, emptyDir data) or enlarge it.

Cordoned.title: Node is cordoned
Cordoned.explanation: spec.unschedulable is set: no new pods are placed on this node; running pods stay. This is the state `kubectl cordon` / a drain leaves the node in.
Cordoned.fix: Uncordon the node once maintenance is done.

LoadBalancerPending.title: Waiting for an external address
LoadBalancerPending.explanation: A Service of type LoadBalancer needs a cloud or on-prem load-balancer controller to assign an address. Without one it stays pending forever.
LoadBalancerPending.fix: On minikube run `minikube tunnel`; on bare metal install MetalLB or use NodePort/Ingress instead.

NoAddress.title: No ingress controller has taken this Ingress
NoAddress.explanation: An Ingress only has effect when an ingress controller watches it. No controller has reported an address, so the rules are not served.
NoAddress.fix: Install an ingress controller and set ingressClassName to its class (or mark the class default).

Terminating.title: Being deleted
Terminating.explanation: deletionTimestamp is set. The object disappears once its finalizers are cleared and its pods have stopped. A Namespace or object stuck here usually has a finalizer whose controller is not running.
Terminating.fix: Wait for the grace period; if it never finishes, check the object's finalizers and the controller responsible for them.

ScaledToZero.title: Scaled to zero
ScaledToZero.explanation: The workload asks for 0 replicas, so there are no pods by design. Nothing is wrong, nothing is running.
ScaledToZero.fix: Scale up to run it again.

Paused.title: Rollout paused
Paused.explanation: spec.paused is true: template changes are recorded but not rolled out until the Deployment is resumed.

ScalingInactive.title: Autoscaler cannot compute a target
ScalingInactive.explanation: The HPA cannot read the metric — usually no metrics-server, or the pods have no CPU/memory REQUESTS (utilization is a percentage of the request).
ScalingInactive.fix: Install metrics-server and set resource requests on the target's containers.
